best_lineage.idea: Replace the naive i-j-k triple loop with a parallel i-k-j implementation: zero C once, split row blocks across std::thread workers, stream rows of B and C, and vectorize the inner j-loop with NEON FMA (vld1q/vfmaq/vst1q) with a scalar tail for non-multiple-of-4 sizes.

Add k-cache blocking (BK=64) to the parallel i-k-j matmul by reordering loops to k-block → i → k → j, so B rows in a k-block are reused across all i rows in a thread's row range instead of being reloaded for every i. This matches the best-known approach (BK=64 → ~85 GFLOPS). BK is made a constexpr for sweeping.
